brief: A strawberry tower for a small balcony: one planter three storeys tall in the middle, ringed by six planters two storeys tall. Fill every planter with soil and plant strawberries in all seven, with a fruiting plant in the middle one.

requirements.requirement: one planter three storeys tall in the middle

requirements.evidence: six 2-storey fused bases around centre, each with hex-bin-full-drain-x2 planter bin
requirements.requirement: ringed by six planters two storeys tall

requirements.evidence: fill_and_plant filled soil in all 7 bins
strawberry-young planted in the six ring bins (prop:2-7)
strawberry-harvest (fruiting stage) planted in middle bin (prop:1)
requirements.requirement: fruiting plant in the middle one

finish.summary: Strawberry tower: 3-storey centre planter with fruiting strawberry plus six 2-storey ring planters with young strawberries, all soiled and planted. House rules capped and locked; checks clear.

lines.label: Bin, full depth, drained, 2 stories deep
Bin, full depth, drained, 3 stories deep
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Building your strawberry tower — a tall centre ringed by six planters, all fruited.
